eaves: The lower edges of the top of a house, reaching out beyond the wall.
take to: To begin to do something often, as a new way of spending time.
bowl over: To hit someone so that they fall down.
turn up: To come, often when no one expected it.
down at heel: Worn down at the back where your foot goes in, as old things worn on the feet are.
get on one's nerves: To make someone feel worried and cross.
come on: Words that tell someone to be quick or to come with you.
make it hot for: To make a person's life hard, as a way to punish them.
pass the time: To spend your time doing something.
make out: To see or hear something that is hard to see or hear.
cast off: To let go the rope that holds a boat, so that it can move away.
take sides: To be with one person against another in a fight or talk.
turn over a new leaf: To start to act in a better way.
egg on: To make someone do something by telling them to do it again and again.
stir your stumps: To be quick; to start moving.
